overview.description: Trionfetti is a four-player partnership game from the rural area between Venice and Padua, played with an Italian suited 40- or 52-card deck. It is a relative of Truc and Put: the aim is to win at least two of three tricks per hand. The cutter (to dealer's left) freely chooses and announces the card ranking (comanda) for each smazzata; four consecutive hands are played from the same deck so players gain information across hands. First team to 20 points wins a game; first to 3 games wins the match.

history.origins: Trionfetti is a four-player partnership game from the rural area between Venice and Padua, played with an Italian suited deck (Trevigiane pattern). It was formally described by Alberto Fiorin at the IPCS Convention in 1997 and is the subject of a booklet by Gianluca Angi (2020). During the 1970s and 1980s several large tournaments were held; in 2009 the Club del 15 in Fossò founded the Scuola di Trionfetti, which still runs weekly meetings to teach new players. The game is a relative of Truc and Put and is preserved as a regional Venetian tradition.

setup.deck: 40- or 52-card Italian deck (Trevigiane). Default ranking ascending: 1 (low) to King (high); 40-card lacks 8s, 9s, 10s.
setup.dealing: Deal 3 cards each per hand. Same dealer deals up to 4 hands from the deck (smazzata). Cutter (to dealer's left) sees cut card and announces ranking (comanda) for the smazzata.

rules.objective: Win at least two of three tricks per hand to score 1 point (or more if vagaresto is accepted). First team to 20 points wins the game; first to 3 games wins the match.
rules.gameplay: Play is anticlockwise. Player to dealer's right leads. No requirement to follow suit; each trick is won by the highest card according to the current ranking (comanda). Ties go to the first played of equal cards. Optional vagaresto raises the stake for the hand. Up to 4 hands (smazzata) from the same deck; then new dealer shuffles and new cutter announces ranking.
keyRules: Cutter announces card ranking (comanda) for each smazzata
No follow suit; highest by ranking wins trick
20 points to win game; 3 games to win match

strategy.basic: Lead strong cards when partner can support; coordinate via allowed signals after first trick.
strategy.intermediate: Coordinate with partner. Win key tricks; consider vagaresto when hand and information justify it.
strategy.advanced: Memory across four hands from same deck; choose comanda (ranking) to favour your side when cutting.

edgeCases.text: Tie for highest card: first played of equal cards wins the trick.
Vagaresto: optional stake raise; opponents may accept or concede; if conceded, calling team scores 1 point.
Communication between partners allowed after first trick of each hand; conventional signals (e.g. padrona, alba) may be used.

engine.handRankingSystem: Tricks won by highest card under current ranking; no poker-style hand ranks.
engine.deckDescription: A 40-card Italian deck (Trevigiane or Venete pattern), often used for Trionfetti; 52-card packs of the same pattern are also available. The 40-card pack omits 8s, 9s and 10s. Four suits with traditional Italian names and imagery; ranking is chosen by the cutter (comanda) and can vary each smazzata.
engine.suitDescription: Four Italian suits: swords (spade or strette), batons (bastoni), cups (coppe), and coins (denari), as in the Trevigiane or Venetian pattern used in the Veneto and Padua area for games such as Trionfetti and Put.
engine.rankDescription: In the 40-card pack the ranks are 1 (ace) through 7 plus Jack (fante), Horse (cavallo), and King (re). Default ascending order is 1 (lowest) to King (highest). The cutter announces the ranking (comanda) for each smazzata, so order can change.
engine.dealPattern: 3 cards each per hand; same dealer deals up to 4 hands from the deck (smazzata); 4 cards remain undealt.
